defs.def: a sudden feeling of great fear that cannot be controlled and prevents you from thinking clearly 惊恐；恐慌

ex.s: As night fell, panic set in.
The man stood up in a panic, then ran through the house toward the window and jumped out.
ex.t: 那名男子惊慌地站起来，然后穿过屋子朝窗户跑去并跳了出去。

ex.s: She searched the faces of her classmates for signs of panic.
ex.t: 当某事与他们的观点矛盾时，他们不会将其视为例外。

ex.s: I looked at them in panic.
When you hear a word that you don’t recognise, don’t panic!
ex.t: 当你听到一个不认识的词时，不要慌张！

ex.s: When listening to instructions in English, you should • listen carefully and don’t panic.
ex.t: 听英语指令时，你应该• 认真听，不要惊慌。

ex.s: This was no time to panic.

defs.def: a situation in which people are made to feel very anxious, causing them to act quickly and without thinking carefully 人心惶惶的局面；惶恐不安

ex.s: Are they there?” in a tone of voice which revealed a sort of panic fear.
ex.t: 「他们在那里吗？」那语气透露出一种惊慌恐惧。
